source_text: Ο ΠΡΟΣ ΤΟΥΣ ΑΝΤΙΟΧΕΙΣ ΤΟΜΟΣ ΑΘΑΝΑΣΙΟΥ ΑΡΧΙΕΠΙΣΚΟΠΟΥ ΑΛΕΞΑΝΔΡΕΙΑΣ. Τοῖς ἀγαπητοῖς καὶ ποθεινοτάτοις συλλειτουργοῖς Εὐσεβίῳ, Λουκίφερι, Ἀστερίῳ, Κυματίῳ καὶ Ἀνατολίῳ, Ἀθανάσιος καὶ οἱ παρατυχόντες ἐν Ἀλεξανδρείᾳ ἐπίσκοποι ἀπό τε τῆς Ἰταλίας καὶ Ἀραβίας, Αἰγύπτου καὶ Λιβύης, Εὐσέβιος, Ἀστέριος, Γάϊος, Ἀγαθὸς, Ἀμμώνιος, Ἀγαθοδαίμων, Δρακότιος, Ἀδέλφιος, Ἑρμαίων, Μάρκος, Θεόδωρος, Ἀνδρέας, Παφνούτιος, ἄλλος Μάρκος, Ζώϊλος, Μη νᾶς, Γεώργιος, Λούκιος, Μακάριος, καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ, ἐν Χριστῷ πλεῖστα χαίρειν. Πεπείσμεθα μὲν, ὅτι, λειτουργοὶ Θεοῦ καὶ οἰκο νόμοι καλοὶ τυγχάνοντες, ἱκανοί ἐστε πρὸς ἅπαντα τὰ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας ἁρμόζεσθαι· ἐπειδὴ δὲ καὶ εἰς ἡμᾶς ἦλθεν, ὅτι πλεῖστοι πρότερον διὰ φιλονεικίαν διαιρεθέντες ἀφ' ἡμῶν, νῦν εἰρηνεύειν βούλονται, πολλοὶ δὲ, καὶ τῆς πρὸς τοὺς Ἀρειομανίτας σχέσεως ἀποστάντες, ἀντιποιοῦνται τῆς πρὸς ἡμᾶς κοινω νίας· ἀναγκαῖον ἡγησάμεθα ταῦθ' ἅπερ ἐγράψαμεν ἡμεῖς τε καὶ οἱ ἀγαπητοὶ ἡμῶν Εὐσέβιός τε καὶ Ἀστέριος, γράψαι τῇ ὑμῶν χρηστότητι, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἀγαπητοὶ καὶ ὡς ἀληθῶς ποθεινότατοι συλλειτουργοὶ, χαίροντες μὲν ἐπὶ τῇ τοιαύτῃ ἀκοῇ, εὐχόμενοι δὲ ἵνα καὶ, εἴ τις ἔτι περιλείπεται μακρὰν ἀφ' ἡμῶν, καὶ εἴ τις ἔτι τοῖς Ἀρειανοῖς συνερχόμενος φαίνεται, οὗτος ἀποπηδήσῃ τῆς ἐκείνων μανίας· ὥστε πάντας πανταχοῦ λοιπὸν λέγειν· «Εἷς Κύριος, μία πίστις.» Τί γὰρ οὕτω «καλὸν,» ὡς ὁ Ὑμνῳδὸς εἶπεν, ἢ τί «τερπνὸν» ἀλλ' ἢ «τὸ κατοικεῖν ἀδελφοὺς ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό;» Οἶκος δὲ ἡμῶν ἡ Ἐκκλησία· καὶ φρόνημα εἶναι πρέπει τὸ αὐτό· οὕτω γὰρ πιστεύομεν καὶ τὸν Κύριον μεθ' ἡμῶν κατοικήσειν λέγοντα· «Ἐνοικήσω ἐν αὐ τοῖς καὶ ἐμπεριπατήσω,» καὶ, «Ὧδε κατοικήσω, ὅτι ᾑρετισάμην αὐτήν.» Ὧδε δὲ ποῦ, ἢ ἔνθα μία πί στις καὶ εὐσέβεια κηρύσσεται; Ἐβουλόμεθα μὲν οὖν ἀληθῶς καὶ ἡμεῖς οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Αἰγύπτου ἅμα τοῖς ἀγαπητοῖς ἡμῶν ἀδελφοῖς Εὐσεβίῳ καὶ Ἀστερίῳ διὰ πολλὰ μὲν, μάλιστα δὲ τούτου χάριν ἐλθεῖν, ἵν' ἅμα τὴν ὑμετέραν περιπτυξώμεθα διάθεσιν, καὶ κοινῇ τῆς τοιαύτης ἀπολαύ σωμεν εἰρήνης τε καὶ ὁμονοίας· ἐπειδὴ δὲ, καθὼς καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἄλλαις ἐπιστολαῖς ἐδηλώσαμεν, καὶ δύνασθε μαθεῖν παρὰ τῶν αὐτῶν συλλειτουργῶν ἡμῶν, αἱ ἐκκλησιαστικαὶ χρεῖαι κατέχουσιν ἡμᾶς· ἐλυ πήθημεν μὲν, ὅμως δὲ ἠξιώσαμεν τοὺς αὐτοὺς συλλειτουργοὺς ἡμῶν Εὐσέβιον καὶ Ἀστέριον ἐλθεῖν ἀνθ' ἡμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς· καὶ χάρις αὐτῶν τῇ θεοσεβείᾳ, ὅτι, καίπερ αὐτοὶ δυνάμενοι σπεύδειν εἰς τὰς παροι κίας ἑαυτῶν, προέκριναν πάντων τὴν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὁδὸν ἕνεκα τῆς κατεπειγούσης ἐκκλησιαστικῆς χρείας. Συνθεμένων οὖν αὐτῶν, παρεμυθησάμεθα ἑαυτοὺς, ὅτι, αὐτῶν τε καὶ ὑμῶν ἐκεῖ τυγχανόντων, πάντες ἑαυτοὺς ἡγούμεθα συνεῖναι ὑμῖν. Πάντας τοίνυν τοὺς βουλομένους εἰρηνεύειν πρὸς ἡμᾶς, καὶ μάλιστα τοὺς ἐν τῇ Παλαιᾷ συναγομένους, καὶ τοὺς ἀποτρέχοντας δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν Ἀρειανῶν προσκαλέσασθε παρ' ἑαυτοῖς, καὶ ὡς μὲν πατέρες υἱοὺς προσλάβεσθε, ὡς δὲ διδάσκαλοι καὶ κηδεμόνες ἀποδέξασθε, καὶ συνάψαντες αὐτοὺς τοῖς ἀγαπητοῖς ἡμῶν τοῖς περὶ Παυλῖνον, μηδὲν πλέον ἀπαιτήσητε παρ' αὐτῶν ἢ ἀναθεματίζειν μὲν τὴν Ἀρειανὴν αἵρεσιν, ὁμολογεῖν δὲ τὴν παρὰ τῶν ἁγίων Πατέρων ὁμολογηθεῖσαν ἐν Νικαίᾳ πίστιν, ἀναθεμα τίζειν δὲ καὶ τοὺς λέγοντας κτίσμα εἶναι τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, καὶ διῃρημένον ἐκ τῆς οὐσίας τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
thought_title: Greeting and the terms for receiving those who seek peace
orientation: Athanasius and the bishops with him in Alexandria open the letter to the Antiochene leaders, urging them to receive those who want peace on the sole condition that they condemn the Arian heresy, confess Nicaea, and reject calling the Holy Spirit a creature.
pass_a_gloss: The Tome to the Antiochenes of Athanasius Archbishop of Alexandria. To the beloved and most longed-for fellow ministers Eusebius, Lucifer, Asterius, Cymatius and Anatolius, Athanasius and the bishops who happened to be present in Alexandria from Italy and Arabia, Egypt and Libya, Eusebius, Asterius, Gaius, Agathos, Ammonius, Agathodaemon, Dracontius, Adelphius, Hermaeon, Marcus, Theodore, Andreas, Paphnutius, another Marcus, Zoilus, Menas, George, Lucius, Macarius, and the rest, very much greeting in Christ. We have been persuaded that, being ministers of God and good stewards, you are sufficient to be fitted to all the affairs of the Church; but since it also came to us that very many who formerly were divided from us through love of strife now wish to make peace, and many, having also departed from association with the Arians, claim communion with us; we considered it necessary to write to your goodness these things which we wrote, both we and our beloved Eusebius and Asterius, and you yourselves, beloved and truly most longed-for fellow ministers, rejoicing at such a report, and praying that, if anyone still remains far from us, and if anyone still appears assembling with the Arians, this one may leap away from their madness; so that all everywhere may henceforth say: 'One Lord, one faith.' For what is so 'good,' as the Psalmist said, or what 'pleasant' but 'the dwelling of brothers together'? And our house is the Church; and it is fitting that the mind be the same; for thus we believe that the Lord will dwell with us, saying: 'I will dwell in them and walk among them,' and, 'Here I will dwell, because I have chosen her.' And here where, or where one faith and piety is proclaimed? We truly wished then that we also, those from Egypt, together with our beloved brothers Eusebius and Asterius, for many reasons, but especially for the sake of this, to come, so that together we might embrace your disposition, and in common enjoy such peace and concord; but since, as we also made clear in the other letters, and you are able to learn from our same fellow ministers, the ecclesiastical needs hold us back; we were grieved, but nevertheless we asked our same fellow ministers Eusebius and Asterius to come in our place to you; and thanks be to their piety, because, although they themselves were able to hasten to their own dioceses, they preferred above all the road to you for the sake of the pressing ecclesiastical need. When they agreed then, we consoled ourselves, because, while they and you are there, we all consider ourselves to be present with you. Call to yourselves then all who wish to make peace with us, and especially those who assemble in the Old Church, and those who are running away from the Arians, and as fathers receive them as sons, and as teachers and guardians welcome them, and having joined them to our beloved ones around Paulinus, require nothing more from them than to condemn the Arian heresy, and to confess the faith confessed by the holy Fathers in Nicaea, and to condemn also those who say that the Holy Spirit is a creature, and divided from the being of Christ.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'condemn' for this term, avoiding the technical-sounding 'anathematize'.
The glossary gives 'confession' for ὁμολογία; the verb is rendered consistently as 'confess' to match the creedal context.
The glossary requires 'creature' for κτίσμα, rejecting 'creation'.
The glossary requires 'being' for οὐσία, rejecting 'essence' and 'ousia'.
The glossary requires 'Old Church' for Παλαιᾷ, rejecting 'Palaea'.
The glossary requires 'Arians' for Ἀρειομανῖται, rejecting 'Ariomaniacs' and 'Arius's followers'.

pass_b_english: The Tome of Athanasius, Archbishop of Alexandria, to the Antiochenes. To our beloved and most longed-for fellow ministers Eusebius, Lucifer, Asterius, Cymatius, and Anatolius: Athanasius and the bishops who happened to be present in Alexandria from Italy and Arabia, Egypt and Libya—Eusebius, Asterius, Gaius, Agathos, Ammonius, Agathodaemon, Dracontius, Adelphius, Hermaeon, Marcus, Theodore, Andreas, Paphnutius, another Marcus, Zoilus, Menas, George, Lucius, Macarius, and the rest—send abundant greetings in Christ.

We are persuaded that, since you are ministers of God and good stewards, you are capable of managing all the affairs of the Church. But since word has reached us that many who were formerly divided from us through love of strife now wish to make peace, and many who have withdrawn from association with the Arians now claim fellowship with us, we considered it necessary to write to your goodness the very things that we and our beloved Eusebius and Asterius have written. We ourselves, beloved and truly most longed-for fellow ministers, rejoice at such news, and we pray that if anyone still remains far from us, and if anyone still appears to be gathering with the Arians, that person may leap away from their madness, so that all people everywhere may at last say, "One Lord, one faith" (Ephesians 4:5). For what is so "good," as the Psalmist said, or what is "pleasant," except "for brothers to dwell together in unity" (Psalm 133:1)? Our house is the Church, and our mind should be the same. For in this way we believe that the Lord will dwell with us, as he says, "I will dwell in them and walk among them" (2 Corinthians 6:16), and, "Here I will dwell, for I have chosen her" (Psalm 132:14). And where is "here," except where one faith and true piety are proclaimed?

We from Egypt truly wished, together with our beloved brothers Eusebius and Asterius, to come for many reasons, but especially for this one: so that we might embrace your disposition and together enjoy such peace and harmony. But since, as we made clear in our other letters—and you can learn this from our fellow ministers themselves—ecclesiastical needs hold us back, we were grieved. Nevertheless, we asked our fellow ministers Eusebius and Asterius to come to you in our place. And thanks be to their piety, because although they could have hurried to their own dioceses, they preferred the journey to you above all things on account of the pressing ecclesiastical need. Since they agreed, we consoled ourselves with this thought: that while they and you are there, we consider all of ourselves to be present with you.

Call to yourselves, then, all who wish to make peace with us—especially those who gather in the Old Church, and also those who are turning away from the Arians. Receive them as fathers receive sons, welcome them as teachers and guardians, and join them to our beloved ones around Paulinus. Require nothing more from them than this: that they condemn the Arian heresy, confess the faith that was confessed by the holy Fathers at Nicaea, and condemn also those who say that the Holy Spirit is a creature and divided from the being of Christ.

last_rejected.why: Source attributes quote to 'the Psalmist' (ὁ Ὑμνῳδός), not to Psalm 133:1 specifically; the citation format misrepresents the source's attribution.
last_rejected.fix: as the Psalmist said, or what is 'pleasant,' except 'for brothers to dwell together in unity'
last_rejected.ruling: ὁ Ὑμνῳδός means 'the Psalmist'; adding Psalm 133:1 as Scripture reference is standard translator practice, not an error.

last_rejected.quote: and condemn also those who say that the Holy Spirit is a creature and divided from the being of Christ

last_rejected.why: Source says 'divided from the being of Christ' (ἐκ τῆς οὐσίας τοῦ Χριστοῦ), but English omits 'of Christ', changing whose being the Spirit is divided from.
last_rejected.fix: and condemn also those who say that the Holy Spirit is a creature and divided from the being of Christ
last_rejected.ruling: English 'the being of Christ' correctly renders τῆς οὐσίας τοῦ Χριστοῦ; 'of Christ' (τοῦ Χριστοῦ) is present, not omitted.
